items.title: 10.21 Feasibility of redox reactions from the activity series or reaction data

source_refs.note: Topic 10.21, printed page 238. The printed '+0.080 V' for silver and the printed sum are noted; Quick Check 10.9 items are used in 10.17.3, 10.18 and 10.19.

blocks.text: The activity series is a reactivity series of metals from highest to lowest; it is used to determine the products of single displacement reactions, in which metal M1 replaces another metal M2 in solution if M1 is higher in the series. From the series we can decide whether a reaction is feasible: we sum the potentials of the half-reactions, and if the cell potential is positive the reaction is possible, if negative it is not. For Fe2+(aq) + 2e- giving Fe(s), E = -0.44 V, and Ag+(aq) + e- giving Ag(s), E = +0.80 V, the overall reaction Fe(s) + 2Ag+(aq) giving Fe2+(aq) + 2Ag(s) has E cell = 0.80 - (-0.44) = +1.24 V, positive, so the reaction is feasible. Another example: Al3+(aq) + 3e- giving Al(s), E = -1.66 V, and Ag+ + e- giving Ag, +0.80 V; for Al3+(aq) + Ag(s) giving Al(s) + Ag+(aq) the sum -1.66 + 0.80 = -0.86 V is negative, so the reaction is not feasible.
